lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Susan, this is Pierre. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than last week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the vegetables?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 2 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: By 10 o'clock I'm starving. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Nights are the hard part.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You can't be eating at 10 at night.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, easy for you to say.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat breakfast every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the vegetables fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to finish eating by 8 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 9 and not a 6?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, if I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Susan, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

score.summary: Susan's coach shows good moments of affirmation and an open-ended goal-setting exchange that ended with a self-chosen goal. However, the coach repeatedly persuades and lectures (lines 37, 43) and does not respond to change talk such as Susan's 'I don't want to end up like my dad' (line 44).
strengths: Line 14: affirmed Susan's persistence on a hard week, which built rapport.
Line 20 and 22: asked permission before offering the fasting-fluid idea, respecting autonomy.
Line 45 and 46: open question led Susan to set her own goal (finish eating by 8 on 4 nights).
coaching_tips: Line 37 and 43: 'You can't be eating at 10' and 'The research is very clear' are persuading; replace with a reflection or ask permission first.
Line 36 and 44: Susan voiced ability and personal reasons for change; reflect these back (e.g., 'You've done this before and you don't want to end up like your dad') before moving to a plan.
Line 35 and 41: respond to barriers with exploration rather than an immediate suggestion; try 'What's one thing that's worked for you before?'
Line 16 and 17: sustain talk was met with reflection, but consider exploring importance and confidence with a scaled question before proposing ideas.
Line 53: close with a brief summary of the goal and barriers before the next-contact plan.
